page: Amazon Web Services c7i.metal-48xl is a bare-metal, compute-optimized server featuring dedicated Intel Xeon 8488C processors. It is equipped with 192 vCPUs across 96 physical cores operating at a clock speed of 3.2 GHz. The system includes 384.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, yielding a 2.0 GB memory-per-core ratio. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, relying instead on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps.

Benchmark results place this server in the top tier (top 10%) for multi-core CPU performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 171,174.13 and a Passmark CPU score of 125,745.92. The processor's support for advanced vector and matrix extensions (AVX-512 and AMX) drives top-tier performance in extended instructions, encryption, and software compilation. Memory read bandwidth is also in the top tier, reaching 13,985.92 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 423.72 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, though overall Passmark memory scores fall into the average category.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the bare-metal architecture provides direct hardware access without hypervisor overhead, maximizing the utility of the 192 dedicated vCPUs. However, the 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio represents a tradeoff for memory-intensive applications, and the lack of local storage requires external storage configurations. This server is optimized for heavy compute workloads, including software compilation, ray tracing, high-throughput web serving, and CPU-based LLM inference.
